chunks: My father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated that Abdullah ibn Aamir ibn Sa'd narrated from Abdul Rahman ibn Abi Najran who said:

Abul Hassan Ar-Ridha (peace be upon him) wrote a letter to some of his companions which he read to me. It said, 'We know the man when we see him, by the reality of faith and by the reality of hypocrisy.'

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ: Abu al-Hasan, a kunya (honorific name) of Imam Ar-Ridha
key_terms.الرِّضَا: The title of the eighth Imam, Musa ibn Ja'far, meaning 'The Contented One'
key_terms.حَقِيقَةِ النِّفَاقِ: The reality or essence of hypocrisy
key_terms.حَقِيقَةِ الْإِيمَانِ: The reality or essence of faith

ai.seo_question: How does Imam Ar-Ridha recognize true faith and hypocrisy in people?
ai.summary: In this letter to his companion, Imam Ar-Ridha (peace be upon him) asserts that he possesses the innate ability to discern the 'reality' (haqiqah) of faith and hypocrisy in individuals merely by sight, a claim rooted in the Shia doctrine of the Imam's infallible spiritual perception. This insight is not merely psychological but is considered a divine gift (karamah) that allows the Imam to see beyond outward appearances to the inner state of the heart, distinguishing true believers from hypocrites with certainty.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 53-1 (The author of the book narrated) my father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’d ibn Abdullah quoted on the authority of Abdullah ibn Aamir ibn Sa’d, on the authority of Abdul Rahman ibn Abi Najran, “
Abul Hassan Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.) wrote a letter to some of his companions which he read to me. It said, ‘We know (all about) men when we see them. We recognize their true faithfulness or hypocrisy.’”
